newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish 1997 GDP seen rising 3.3 pct -BCH.
newsitem.headline: Spanish 1997 GDP seen rising 3.3 pct -BCH.

text.p: The research department of Spain's Banco Central Hispano (BCH) has upgraded its forecast for 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 3.3 percent from 2.7 percent on the basis of buoyant private consumption and capital goods investment.

In a research note on Thursday, BCH said the fall in the inflation rate and the public deficit had lifted Spain's chances of entering the first round of European Economic and Monetary Union to 90 percent.
Acceptance of Spain's EMU candidacy and a fall key interest rates were determining factors in a domestic demand recovery, the bank said.
It estimated private consumption growth at 2.6 percent in the first quarter and forecast a 3.2 percent growth rate for the second quarter.

The National Statistic Institute INE said GDP rose a provisional 2.6 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter of 1996, while the Bank of Spain has estimated that GDP grew around 2.7 percent in the first quarter.
The government's target for GDP growth this year is 3.0 percent.
